## 🎯 Objectives

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

* use `reactlog` to inspect a Shiny dependency graph;
* replace repeated calculations with one shared reactive expression;
* add a package function that launches a Shiny app; and
* audit an app before web deployment.

## 1. Clone and run the app (5 minutes)

Clone the workshop repository and open `wplshare.Rproj`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/numbats/etc5523-wpl-share.git
cd etc5523-wpl-share
```

Install any packages you do not already have:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "bslib", "devtools", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "reactlog", "rsconnect", "shiny"
))
```

Start a fresh R session, enable reactive logging, and run the app:

```r
reactlog::reactlog_enable()
shiny::runApp("inst/app")
```

Change both inputs and check the number, plot and table.

## 2. Inspect the current graph (10 minutes)

With the app running, open the reactive log:

* macOS: **Cmd + F3**
* Windows/Linux: **Ctrl + F3**

Find `input$season`, `input$minimum_runs` and the four outputs. The log may also
contain browser and layout nodes; use search or double-click an output to isolate
its dependency family.

Then return to the app and set **Minimum runs** to exactly 150 in season
2024/25. Compare the number, plot and table before inspecting `app.R`.

Answer:

1. Why does the table disagree with the other outputs?
2. Why do both inputs connect directly to every output in `reactlog`?

::: {.callout-note}
If the keyboard shortcut does not work, stop the app and run
`shiny::reactlogShow()` in the console.
:::

::: {.unilur-solution}
## What the first run reveals

The number and plot use `runs >= input$minimum_runs`, while the table uses
`runs > input$minimum_runs`. JL Jonassen has exactly 150 runs in 2024/25, so the
table omits a batter counted and plotted elsewhere.

Each output contains its own filter and reads both inputs directly. There is no
shared reactive node between the inputs and outputs.
:::

## 3. Put the filter in one place (15 minutes)

Add this labelled reactive expression at the top of `server()`:

```r
selected_batters <- reactive({
  batters |>
    filter(
      season == input$season,
      runs >= input$minimum_runs
    )
}, label = "selected_batters")
```

Replace the repeated filtering code in all four outputs with calls to
`selected_batters()`.

Run the app and repeat the 150-run test. Then stop the app, clear the old log,
run it again, and change one input:

```r
shiny::reactlogReset()
shiny::runApp("inst/app")
```

Reopen `reactlog`. Identify which nodes depend on `selected_batters` and step
through what happens after the input changes.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Refactored server

```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  selected_batters <- reactive({
    batters |>
      filter(
        season == input$season,
        runs >= input$minimum_runs
      )
  }, label = "selected_batters")

  output$number_shown <- renderText({
    nrow(selected_batters())
  })

  output$leading_batter <- renderText({
    selected <- selected_batters()
    req(nrow(selected) > 0)
    selected$striker[which.max(selected$runs)]
  })

  output$batters_plot <- renderPlot({
    selected_batters() |>
      ggplot(aes(
        x = dot_percent,
        y = boundary_percent,
        size = balls_faced
      )) +
      geom_point(colour = "#006DAE", alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(
        x = "Dot-ball percentage",
        y = "Boundary percentage",
        size = "Balls faced"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
  })

  output$batters_table <- renderTable({
    selected_batters() |>
      arrange(desc(runs)) |>
      select(striker, batting_team, runs, balls_faced) |>
      head(5)
  })
}
```

Both inputs now feed `selected_batters`; all four outputs depend on that shared
node. When an input changes, the shared reactive and its downstream outputs are
invalidated.
:::

## 4. Make the app launchable from the package (12 minutes)

The repository already has the structure of an R package. Files under
`inst/app` will be installed with it.

Create `R/run_app.R`, then add a documented, exported `run_app()` function:

```r
usethis::use_r("run_app")
```

The function should:

1. locate the installed `app` directory with `system.file()`; and
2. pass that directory to `shiny::runApp()`.

Generate the documentation, install the package and test the launcher:

```r
devtools::document()
devtools::install()
wplshare::run_app()
```

Why would a path such as `/Users/name/wpl-share/inst/app` fail for another
package user?

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Package launcher

```r
#' Run the WPL batting explorer
#'
#' @return No return value; called for its side effect of launching the app.
#' @export
run_app <- function() {
  app_dir <- system.file("app", package = "wplshare")
  shiny::runApp(app_dir)
}
```

`inst/app` becomes `app` at the top level of the installed package.
`system.file()` finds that location in the active R library rather than assuming
where the source repository exists on a particular computer.
:::

## 5. Audit the web deployment (10 minutes)

Treat the hosting service as a clean Linux computer that receives only the app
bundle. Mark each item **ready**, **not ready**, or **not applicable**:

* all required files are inside `inst/app`;
* file paths are relative and match the exact case of the file names;
* package dependencies can be detected from the app code;
* there is no `install.packages()` call in the app;
* no password, token or secret is stored in the repository;
* every possible input state produces a useful response; and
* any durable writes use storage outside the app's local filesystem.

Ask `rsconnect` what it detects:

```r
rsconnect::appDependencies("inst/app")
```

Which audit item does the current app handle least well? If time permits, make
one improvement and rerun the app.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Audit findings

The data are bundled under `inst/app/data`, paths are relative, packages are
loaded explicitly, and the source contains no installation calls or secrets.

The empty selection is poorly communicated. `req()` prevents an error in the
leader box but leaves it blank. One possible replacement is:

```r
output$leading_batter <- renderText({
  selected <- selected_batters()

  if (nrow(selected) == 0) {
    return("No batter meets this threshold")
  }

  selected$striker[which.max(selected$runs)]
})
```

A deployed app should use a database, object store or other persistent service
for durable writes because hosted instances can restart or be replaced.
:::
